name: San José

sources.title: Phys.org (2022) — Colombia shares unprecedented images of treasure-laden wreck (four campaigns by the Colombian Navy: cannons partly covered in mud, porcelain, bottles, pottery, gold)
Live Science — $17 billion shipwreck near Colombia is remarkably preserved (intact porcelain in the remains of the hull; bronze guns cast with dolphins)
Divernet — Items lifted from San José shipwreck: the first objects raised from the upper layers of the debris field at about 600 m
San José (ship) — Spanish galleon sunk in Wager's Action on 8 June 1708

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q5874775_san_jose.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/sailkit.py, tools/dresskit.py) with AI assistance. The debris field at about 600 m off the Rosario Islands: the bottom of the hull, below the turn of the bilge, deep in the mud with its frames showing, the rest of the ship blown apart; about four dozen bronze guns half-buried in and around it, Chinese porcelain bowls, glass bottles, jars, gold coins and ingots, and timbers spread by the explosion. Colombia keeps the position secret: the catalog pin is moved some 15 km west of the Wikidata point, to where the GEBCO cells give the real depth of about 600 m (there they give 78 m). The layout of the remains is approximate. model_built.glb: the galleon under sail in 1708. No marine life in the model: Offlined draws the living things itself.
